definitions.check_s: CheckedOutput.check_s is never filled: reported as 'not recorded'
definitions.evidence_triples: ledger field evidence_triples, one value per ledger row (an initial output checked by one source); replay rows (use = replay) cover every checked output of every source; online rows (use = checker or both) are the arms actually run and are never pooled with replay rows; union = sum of its sources' budgets; generic_retry/<arm> = the curated checks
definitions.latency_s: wall_s - checker.retry.started_s of the branch record: on a branch record both come from the prefix clock, retry.started_s is the first live clock read after the replayed initial phase and the check, so the interval is the live retry phase only (model calls, tool calls, store waits, query-gate waits and the runner's start-gate wait before the first live request included; model_call_s is the model requests alone). A negative value (clock inconsistency) is left out of the latency series and counted in the diagnostics
definitions.live_retry_turns: the per-turn entries after the replayed prefix; the prefix is the parent record's whole per_turn list (checked equal by hash, parent found by checker.branched_from in the same OUT); also required: the count equals checker.retry.turns, turn numbers run 1..N, and the prefix turns start no later than checker.retry.started_s while every live turn starts no earlier
definitions.median_p90: linear interpolation between order statistics (type 7, statistics.quantiles method inclusive); n = 0 is 'not estimable'; n = 1 gives that value
definitions.model_call_s: sum of the live retry turns' latency_s (the model requests' own latency, no tool or store time)
definitions.model_keys: the model id of the record or ledger row, lower-cased with every run of other characters as '-'
definitions.retried_answer: a branch record whose checker.retry is present (the checker flagged the initial answer and a live retry ran, or was started: retry.turns may be 0 when the first live request failed, such an answer has no live tokens and its latency is the time that request took; diagnostics count them); the answer is counted once, in the cell of the record. A claim digest names one attempt: where several checker records in records/ share one, the record no other names in runner.infra_try_run_ids is the attempt's, and a group that does not resolve to exactly one is left out and counted in the diagnostics
definitions.zero_live_turns: a retried answer whose first live request failed has retry.turns 0: its tokens are 0 here, which is a floor (the failed request's own tokens are not recorded); the *_excluding_zero_live_turns series leave these answers out
